title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatic, combinatorial 'Analysis situs' (2nd version). In it an 'atelier' (workshop) is a structure with the following ingredients.
- M is a set of basic 'lieux' or figures, ordered by ≤.
- 𝓕 is a larger class of figures (sups of families of elements of M).
- To each figure X is attached an ordered set X̃. Read X̃ as the elements of M below X, so a figure is recovered as Sup_{Z∈X̃} Z.
- omb(X), the 'ombre' (shadow) of X, is a set of point-like elements.
- X ≭ Y is a compatibility relation between figures. For points it is written x‖y.

The previous page defines a Σ-atelier, for Σ a full subcategory (in effect an isomorphism-closed class) of ordered sets. The conditions are (i) X̃ ∈ Σ for every X ∈ M, and (ii) the axiom stated on this page.

Axiom At 9_Σ, the compatibility criterion by lieux. Let X, Y ∈ M and K = X∩Y = Inf^≤(X,Y) = Sup_{Z∈X̃∩Ỹ} Z, so that K̃ = X̃∩Ỹ. Then X ≭ Y holds if and only if both of the following hold.
- (i) Locality: for every x ∈ omb(X)∖omb(K) and y ∈ omb(Y)∖omb(K), x‖y. That is, the parts of X and Y outside their common part are pointwise compatible.
- (ii) Shape: K̃ ∈ Σ, so the poset of the common part has an allowed shape.

Corollary 1 (the earlier At 9''). If (i) holds and K ∈ M (i.e. K̃ has a greatest element), then X ≭ Y. Proof: K ∈ M gives K̃ ∈ Σ by condition (i) of the definition of Σ-atelier.

Corollary 2 (the earlier At 9'). If Σ contains every ordered set isomorphic to some F̃ with F ∈ 𝓕 (for instance Σ = all ordered sets), then condition (ii) is automatic and X ≭ Y holds if and only if (i) holds.

A struck-out remark says that all the 'stations' he has in mind are Σ-ateliers for a suitable Σ. The tentative choice there is Σ_M, the class of posets isomorphic to some X̃ with X ∈ M.

The rotated margin note says the formalism interpolates between two extreme cases:
- Σ = all ordered sets, where (ii) is empty (Corollary 2);
- Σ = Σ_M, where (ii) is equivalent to K ∈ M (Corollary 1 becomes an equivalence).

Purpose: to unify the scattered axioms At 9, 9', 9'' into one parametrised axiom. The next page uses it to organise the implications among At 9–12 (disjunction, gluing and intersection criteria). There At 11, the gluing for infinite sups, is singled out as the only axiom not implied by At 9_Σ + At 10.
errors: Corollary 1 relies tacitly on Σ ⊇ Σ_M. This is condition (i) of the Σ-atelier definition on the previous page, so the argument is correct but the dependence is implicit.
In Corollary 2 one needs K̃ = X̃∩Ỹ to be isomorphic to F̃ for some F ∈ 𝓕, i.e. K = Sup(X̃∩Ỹ) ∈ 𝓕 with K̃ recovered exactly. This is presumably guaranteed by earlier axioms but is not restated here.
The struck-out remark claims every station is a Σ_M-atelier. Grothendieck crossed it out, apparently because it would force (ii) to coincide with K ∈ M and so exclude non-representable intersections.

ideas.what: Parametrised compatibility axiom: two basic figures are compatible iff their parts outside the intersection are pointwise compatible and the intersection poset lies in a prescribed class Σ
ideas.modern_name: Locality / gluing condition for compatibility in a poset-based (finite-space, fan-like or face-poset) combinatorial topology; loosely analogous to the 'cones meet in a common face' condition for fans
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; general analogues in the combinatorics of fans and regular CW posets (Björner and others)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; the programme of a 'tame topology' is announced only vaguely in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

ideas.what: Interpolation between Σ = all ordered sets and Σ = Σ_M, recovering the older axioms 9' and 9'' as corollaries
ideas.modern_name: Axiom unification / parametrisation by a class of 'allowed shapes'

missed.claim: The 1986 'ateliers / stations' axiomatics for analysis situs, a combinatorial and order-theoretic foundation of tame topology, is an unpublished and unstudied attempt. This page contains its key compatibility axiom At 9_Σ, which is parametrised by a class Σ of admissible intersection-poset shapes. No later literature on o-minimality, finite spaces or stratified spaces appears to have taken up this order-theoretic formulation.
missed.quote: Pour que X ≭ Y, il faut et suffit que (i) ∀x∈omb(X)∖omb(K), y∈omb(Y)∖omb(K), on a x‖y (ii) K̃∈Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with axiomatic tame topology (o-minimal structures), posets of strata and fans. It is of historical interest as Grothendieck's concrete attempt at the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. The page itself, however, is a technical reorganisation of axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical, internal reorganisation of an unpublished axiom system. Its interest is mainly that the whole 'atelier' framework is unknown in the literature; the page itself has no striking result.
transcription_corrections: The heading reads 'At 9_Σ' (Atelier axiom), not 'Ax 9_Σ'; likewise 'ancien At 9''' and 'ancien At 9''.
'pour Σ-dalles' should read 'pour Σ-ateliers'; 'Σ-dalle' in the struck-out remark is likewise 'Σ-atelier'.
'il faut et suffit que' is written in abbreviated form ('il f. et s. que').
The parenthesis after (i) likely reads '(connaissant x ≭ y)' or similar, and remains uncertain.
The margin note likely reads '... deux cas : 1°) Σ = tous les ens. ord., alors cela est vide ; 2°) Σ = Σ_M = cat. ..., alors (ii) équivaut à K ∈ M'.
